The opening contrasts fictional pursuit with a sparse-data geographic prediction task, uses offender avoidance and familiar surroundings to motivate assumptions, then gives two distinct model paragraphs: centroid movement through a kinematic analogy and rational-choice location preference through microeconomic reasoning. Evaluation uses next-crime error distance for the first and a random-search-relative home-location metric for the second; these are different outcomes and baselines. Its claimed utility is qualified by per-series parameter sensitivity and omitted population/geographic features, with experienced police filling those information gaps. A separately labeled Abstract starts later and repeats assumptions and the first model description; retain both source sections rather than automatically deduplicating author text. A page number and title are merged in the candidate and need source ownership review. No statistical, formula or figure validation.
